name: Redis rate limiting and response caching for FastAPI
short_definition: Protect Python HTTP APIs with distributed rate limits and cache hot read responses using Redis as the shared store across workers. Prefer sliding/fixed window limits keyed by user id (authenticated) or IP (anonymous), return 429 with Retry-After, and cache only safe GETs with explicit TTLs and identity-aware keys. As of 2026-07-13: redis-py 8.0.1, limits 5.8.0, slowapi 0.1.10, fastapi-limiter 0.2.0, cashews 7.5.0, hishel 1.3.0.
scope_in: Application-layer rate limiting (per route, per user, per IP)
HTTP response caching for idempotent reads
Cache key design, TTL, invalidation hooks
scope_out: CDN/WAF/edge rate limits (Cloudflare etc.) as primary — complementary
Next.js Upstash patterns (backend-api.md) except interop notes
Full Redis ops (persistence, cluster topology deep dive)

defaults.rate_limit_lib: slowapi + limits Redis storage OR fastapi-limiter / custom Lua token bucket — pick one stack per service
defaults.keying: auth: user_id (or sub); anon: hashed IP + route; never trust raw X-Forwarded-For without proxy trust
defaults.algorithms: sliding window or fixed window for APIs; token bucket for bursty LLM routes
defaults.response_429: status 429, code RATE_LIMIT, optional Retry-After; do not leak internal keys
defaults.order: auth (if required) → rate limit → validate → handler (aligns with backend-api gates)
defaults.cache: cashews or manual redis.get/set for app cache; hishel for outbound HTTP cache
defaults.cache_when: Only GET/HEAD public or per-user responses; never cache authenticated responses under shared keys
defaults.ttl: Short TTLs (seconds–minutes) with explicit invalidation on writes
defaults.local_dev: memory backend OK for single-process; CI must not assume multi-instance fairness

rate_limit_when: Auth, signup, password reset, billing, contact, AI generation, expensive search
Any endpoint abusable for cost amplification
cache_when: Read-heavy reference data with tolerable staleness
Expensive computed GET with invalidation path
Outbound idempotent HTTP (hishel) to third parties
do_not_cache_when: Responses with user PII under global keys
Security-sensitive decisions that must be real-time

alternatives.edge_waf: Cloudflare/nginx limit_req for coarse IP limits
alternatives.upstash_ts: Next BFF uses @upstash/ratelimit; Python uses redis-py against same Redis if shared
alternatives.in_process_aiolimiter: Single-process only; wrong for multi-worker prod

do: Key by authenticated principal first, IP second
Use Redis from lifespan; health-check Redis for readiness if required for correctness
Document limit budgets per route class in OpenAPI/description
Include route name in rate limit key
Invalidate or namespace-bump caches on mutations
Fail policy: decide closed (429/503 if Redis down) vs open (fail-open) explicitly — prefer fail-closed for auth
dont: Don't use pure in-memory limits as the only prod control with multiple workers
Don't rate-limit solely on client-supplied user id header
Don't cache Set-Cookie or Authorization-varying responses without Vary and private keys
Don't infinite TTL without eviction plan
Don't put unbounded request bodies into cache keys
Don't skip limits on 'internal' routes exposed publicly

code_skeleton:
import time
from collections.abc import AsyncIterator, Callable
from contextlib import asynccontextmanager
from typing import Annotated

import redis.asyncio as redis
from fastapi import Depends, FastAPI, HTTPException, Request, status
from pydantic import BaseModel

WINDOW_SEC = 60
LIMIT = 30

@asynccontextmanager
async def lifespan(app: FastAPI) -> AsyncIterator[None]:
    app.state.redis = redis.from_url("redis://localhost:6379/0", decode_responses=True)
    yield
    await app.state.redis.aclose()

app = FastAPI(lifespan=lifespan)

async def get_redis() -> redis.Redis:
    return app.state.redis

RedisDep = Annotated[redis.Redis, Depends(get_redis)]

async def rate_limit_user(r: redis.Redis, *, key: str, limit: int = LIMIT, window: int = WINDOW_SEC) -> None:
    # simple fixed window; production often uses sliding window or INCR+EXPIRE patterns / Lua
    bucket = f"rl:{key}:{int(time.time()) // window}"
    count = await r.incr(bucket)
    if count == 1:
        await r.expire(bucket, window)
    if count > limit:
        raise HTTPException(
            status_code=status.HTTP_429_TOO_MANY_REQUESTS,
            detail={"error": "Too many requests", "code": "RATE_LIMIT"},
            headers={"Retry-After": str(window)},
        )

class Item(BaseModel):
    id: str
    name: str

@app.get("/v1/items/{item_id}")
async def get_item(item_id: str, request: Request, r: RedisDep) -> Item:
    user = request.headers.get("x-user-id", "anon")  # replace with JWT sub
    await rate_limit_user(r, key=f"user:{user}:get_item")
    cache_key = f"cache:item:{item_id}"
    cached = await r.get(cache_key)
    if cached:
        return Item.model_validate_json(cached)
    item = Item(id=item_id, name="demo")  # DB fetch
    await r.set(cache_key, item.model_dump_json(), ex=60)
    return item
failure_modes: In-memory limiter per worker → effective limit × N workers
Redis outage: unhandled exceptions → 500 storms; or silent fail-open abuse
X-Forwarded-For spoofing → wrong tenant limited or attacker bypass
Cache key collision across tenants (IDOR via cache)
Stale cache after write without invalidation
Hot key thundering herd on expiry
Rate limit key cardinality explosion (unique key per request body hash)
anti_patterns: Global single counter for all users
Storing full sensitive payloads in Redis without TTL/encryption policy
slowapi in-memory only in multi-replica k8s

Process-local cachetools as only cache in multi-instance APIs
fastapi-cache2 lightly maintained patterns without review
Fail-open rate limits on login without monitoring
ts_boundary: Next Server Actions use Upstash Ratelimit (backend-api.md). If Python and Next share abuse surface, use consistent key namespaces (e.g. rl:login:user:) and preferably same Redis. Do not double-charge users with unrelated tight limits on BFF and Python without design. Browser never talks to Redis.
rust_boundary: Edge rate limit / high QPS gateways may live in Axum+Redis or infra (envoy). Python app limits remain defense in depth for expensive AI routes.
supabase_boundary: Don't use Postgres as a general rate-limit store (row churn). Redis is appropriate. Cache invalidation on Supabase writes may need webhooks or application-level deletes. Never cache service_role results into a public key space.
boundary_contracts: REDIS_URL in settings; separate DB index for rl vs cache if needed
Document limit tiers per API product
Cache-Control on public GETs when CDN involved

Network ACL + AUTH on Redis; TLS in cloud

Order: auth → rate limit → validate → mutate (backend-api aligned)
